candidate_relations.reason: An expansile unilocular mandibular lesion can fall under bone tumors, but this label does not identify its odontogenic ameloblastomatous and keratinizing character.
Developmental odontogenic cysts were only a radiographic differential, whereas the reference is a keratinizing ameloblastoma variant.
The well-defined unilocular posterior mandibular lesion lacks histologic giant cells or the typical anterior crossing-midline pattern of a central giant cell granuloma.
There are no multiple jaw cysts, basal-cell carcinomas, calcified falx, or family findings to support Gorlin syndrome.
The lesion's cyst-like radiographic appearance prompted this differential, but an odontogenic cyst does not contain the ameloblastomatous tumor component required by keratoameloblastoma.
Unicystic ameloblastoma matches the unilocular expansile imaging pattern but does not specify the keratinizing differentiation that defines keratoameloblastoma.
A solitary posterior mandibular lesion in a 54-year-old woman is unlike childhood-onset bilateral symmetric jaw expansion of cherubism.
The radiolucent expansile process is a jaw lesion, but this phrase provides neither odontogenic tumor lineage nor keratoameloblastoma subtype.
An odontogenic keratocyst can be unilocular in the posterior mandible but lacks the ameloblastomatous neoplastic component of the reference.
Cortical expansion by a discrete mandibular lesion is compatible with a jaw tumor, yet the specific keratinizing ameloblastoma identity is omitted.
Although radiolucent and unilocular, calling the lesion a mandibular cyst excludes the tumor component inherent in keratoameloblastoma.
A developmental odontogenic cyst was considered before excision, but it is a different pathologic class from keratoameloblastoma.

case_quality_flags: No histopathologic findings from the excisional biopsy are included, so the record cannot distinguish keratoameloblastoma from the stated unicystic ameloblastoma and odontogenic-cyst differentials.
